patch.value: Fetch with object negotiation computed from reachability

Fetch must not send the whole object store. The client offers the commits it already has as candidates, the remote keeps only the ones it actually holds, and the bundle it builds excludes everything reachable from that agreed set and declares it as a prerequisite instead. The refs a fetch learns land on tracking refs only. Publishing the remote's own ref names, which is what a plain bundle import does, would move the local branch of the same name onto the remote's tip and silently discard whatever the local agent had committed there.

A fetch into a repository that already shares history transfers strictly fewer objects than a fetch into an empty one; a fetch never writes any ref outside refs/remotes/; a fetch into a repository whose local branch has diverged leaves that local branch untouched; candidate haves the remote does not hold are dropped rather than failing the fetch; fetch records the tracking refs it moved in the operation log
